scope: Fail-fast held-out comparison of zero-shot and metric-control VACE adapter
summary: The adapter improves static contact and global similarity but regresses contact motion and is rejected; remaining held-out clips are not run.
evidence: On unseen contact clip 001, contact ROI similarity rises from 0.170427 to 0.177509 and global similarity rises from 0.246999 to 0.292221.
Contact-motion similarity regresses from 0.821650 to 0.819798, a -0.001852 change, so all_proxy_gates_pass=false.
Adapted and zero-shot videos differ by 7.0669 RGB levels on average, so the result is not a no-op.
Three-timepoint storyboard review shows both generated videos replace the target pink flower with an incorrect green mass; the LoRA is not promoted.
lessons: Physically valid controls and trainability do not guarantee that a small appearance model learns the correct flower identity or dynamics.
A positive static ROI metric cannot override a motion regression or semantic visual veto.
limitations: Only the first unseen contact window is run under the fail-fast rule.
The comparison is synthetic and does not establish real Pexels quality.
next_actions: Do not expand this adapter; require a stronger multi-scene appearance model or paired real/sim supervision before another held-out campaign.
